title: Root morphology: the ByOrder machinery on roots was dead
question: Is this the axis you meant by 'fully different morphology'? And is a descending main axis with wandering laterals the right shape to aim at, or did you mean something else?
context_md:
Your verdict on the last card: *"clearly different but not as much as I
would like. It just looks like more vs less roots instead of fully
different morphology."* That was right, and it pointed at a dead
mechanism.

**Why it could only be density.** Every `ByOrder` field on the root's
`Grow` is a **single-element array** — `upward_weight: [0.6]` — and
`.at(order)` clamps to the last entry. So a primary axis and a
third-order lateral read the *same* parameters. Worse: nothing ever
incremented a root's order. `break_buds` does exactly this above ground
("a flushed bud is an axillary meristem — it is a lateral by definition,
so it starts the next tier"); `break_root_tips` never did, and neither
did my new lateral conversion. **Every root cell in the world is order
0**, so the `ByOrder` machinery on roots has been dead the whole time —
a gate hiding a second bug by making it unreachable.

**Left** is today. **Right** is with laterals incrementing their order,
plus one species-data line authoring a hierarchy
(`upward_weight: [0.95, 0.15]` — primary axis drives down, laterals
wander).

| | today | order + hierarchy |
|---|---|---|
| depth histogram, surface→bedrock | 27, 28, 16, 13, 13 | **15, 21, 22, 20, 19** |
| deepest row below surface | 26.6 | 29.8 |
| lateral spread | 54.6 | 55.0 |
| root cells with 3+ root neighbours | 72% | 67% |

**The control matters here:** the order fix *alone*, with today's uniform
authoring, is **byte-identical** to today — same 438 median, same
histogram, every figure. It changes nothing for any shipped species and
only makes the axis reachable. The morphology comes from the one authored
line.

I have **not** landed the authored hierarchy — that is a species-design
call, and `[0.95, 0.15]` is a first guess I picked to test whether the
axis exists at all.
